findings.title: Invalid Ruby prevents the discussion template from rendering
findings.body: The conditional is closed with `end if` rather than `end`. The trailing `if` has no condition, so the generated ERB Ruby fails to compile. Every embed request that finds an existing topic will fail instead of displaying the discussion. Close the block with `end` and add a test that renders the actual view.

findings.title: Feed imports persist unsanitized HTML as cooked posts
findings.body: Imported contents are parsed by Nokogiri but never sanitized before being saved with the raw_html cook method, which returns the HTML unchanged. PollFeed passes feed content directly into this method, so script tags, event-handler attributes, and dangerous links from a feed become stored executable content on the forum's origin. The source URL is also interpolated into HTML without escaping. Sanitize the final imported HTML, including the attribution link, before bypassing the cooking pipeline.

findings.title: RSS entries without a content element abort feed polling
findings.body: The poller unconditionally calls `scrub` on `i.content`. Valid RSS feeds commonly provide article text in `description` rather than a content element; for those entries, content is nil and polling raises instead of importing the entry. Since the exception exits the loop and retries are disabled, later entries also go unprocessed. Handle missing content and use the appropriate RSS description fallback.

findings.title: Relative URL conversion corrupts protocol-relative links
findings.body: The URL conversion treats every href beginning with `/` as a path on the article host. A valid protocol-relative link such as `//cdn.example.com/file` is consequently rewritten to `http://article-host/cdn.example.com/file`; the image conversion below has the same problem. Path-relative links such as `images/photo.jpg` are not resolved at all and instead point at the forum when rendered there. Resolve references against the full source URI rather than concatenating the source host.

findings.title: Remote retrieval follows redirects outside the allowed embed host
findings.body: TopicRetriever validates only the initial URL's host, then this method fetches it with open-uri, which follows HTTP redirects. An allowed-host URL that redirects to another host can therefore cause the worker to fetch internal HTTP services and publish their extracted content as a topic, bypassing the embedding host restriction. Validate redirect destinations and resolved addresses before each request, rejecting private or otherwise disallowed targets.
